end.summary:
- Practised identifying physical and chemical changes using reversibility and new-substance clues.
- Correctly identified melting ice, dissolving sugar, and melting ghee as physical changes in later responses.
- Identified roasting or burning chapati as chemical because of colour, smell, texture change, and formation of a new substance.
- Teach-back was not passed; the ghee example remained marked as chemical on the child’s screen and was not confirmed as corrected.
end.parentNote: Ananya practised separating physical changes from chemical changes using reversibility and whether a new substance forms. They explained several examples and later consistently described melting ghee as a physical change, while also noticing colour, smell, and texture clues in burnt chapati. The on-screen ghee label caused a mix-up that was not confirmed as corrected during the lesson. At home, ask Ananya to sort everyday examples into two groups and give one reason for each choice.
